name: Sirius
tagline: The Dog Star — brightest star in Earth's night sky, hiding a dead companion.
history: Twice the Sun's mass and 25 times its luminosity, Sirius outshines every other star in the night sky. Ancient Egyptians timed their calendar and predicted the Nile flood by its dawn rising; Greeks blamed its summer heat for the 'dog days'. Its unseen companion was predicted in 1844 when Friedrich Bessel noticed Sirius wobbling, and Alvan Graham Clark spotted Sirius B in 1862 — the first white dwarf ever discovered, an Earth-size ember with the mass of a Sun. That dead star once outshone its partner before collapsing; it remains a cornerstone of stellar-evolution theory.
